q.t: A necklace has 10 shells. How many shells are there on 3 such necklaces?
q.e: Each necklace is one group of ten, so 3 tens = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.

q.t: Manoj has 4 trays with 10 chikoos in each tray and 6 loose chikoos. How many chikoos are there in all?
q.e: 4 trays of ten make 40, and 6 more make 46.

q.t: How many ones make one ten?
q.e: When we have 10 ones, we bundle them into 1 ten.

q.t: In the number 58, what does the 5 stand for?
q.e: The left digit is in the tens place, so 5 means 5 tens = 50.

q.t: Write 7 tens and 2 ones as a number.
q.e: 7 tens is 70, and 2 ones more makes 72.

q.t: Which is more: 43 oranges or 34 oranges?
q.e: 43 has 4 tens but 34 has only 3 tens, so 43 is more.

q.t: How many tens are there in 60?
Which is the smallest two-digit number?
q.e: Two-digit numbers start when we first have 1 ten: 10. Before that, 9 has only one digit.

q.t: Which is the largest two-digit number?
q.e: 9 is the biggest digit, so 9 tens and 9 ones is the biggest. One more is 100, which has three digits.

q.t: In a boat race, the red boat came 1st, the blue boat came 2nd and the green boat came 3rd. Which boat came just after the blue boat?
q.e: After 2nd comes 3rd, and the green boat was 3rd.

q.t: 25 chikoos are put in trays of 10. How many trays are full?
q.e: 25 is 2 tens and 5 ones, so 2 trays are full.

q.t: 25 chikoos are put in trays of 10. How many chikoos are left over, not in a full tray?
q.e: 2 full trays hold 20, and 25 − 20 = 5 are left.

q.t: A ten strip has 10 units. How many ten strips make 100 units?
q.e: 10 tens make 100 — count 10, 20, 30 … 100 and you say ten numbers.

q.t: Which number is 9 tens and 3 ones?
q.e: 9 tens = 90, and 3 ones more makes 93.

q.t: Fill in the blank: 67 is ___ than 76.
q.e: 67 has 6 tens, 76 has 7 tens. Fewer tens means less.

q.t: Which shows 84 broken into tens and ones?
q.e: 84 is 8 tens (80) and 4 ones (4).

q.t: What is the smallest two-digit number with 3 in the tens place?
q.e: With 3 tens fixed, the smallest ones digit is 0, so the number is 30.

q.t: What is the largest two-digit number with 2 in the ones place?
q.e: With 2 ones fixed, the biggest tens digit is 9, so the number is 92.

q.t: Which number is between 47 and 59?
q.e: 52 is bigger than 47 and smaller than 59. The others are outside.

q.t: On a calendar, 15 August is a Tuesday. What day is 16 August?
q.e: The next date is the next day of the week, and Wednesday comes after Tuesday.

q.t: Use the digit cards 3 and 5 once each. What is the bigger number you can make?
q.e: Put the bigger digit, 5, in the tens place: 5 tens beats 3 tens.

q.t: Swap the two digits of 27. What new number do you get?
q.e: The 2 moves to the ones place and the 7 to the tens place: 7 tens and 2 ones = 72.

q.t: What is the largest two-digit number where no digit is repeated?
q.e: 99 repeats the 9, so keep 9 tens and take the next biggest digit, 8, for the ones.

q.t: What is the smallest two-digit number whose two digits are the same?
q.e: 10 has different digits; the first one with matching digits is 11.

q.t: Arrange from biggest to smallest: 53, 35, 50.
q.e: 53 and 50 both have 5 tens; 53 has more ones. 35 has only 3 tens, so it is smallest.

q.t: Which number has 6 ones and 4 tens?
q.e: Tens are written first: 4 tens and 6 ones is 46, not 64.

q.t: 43 oranges go into trays of 10. How many trays do we need so that no orange is left out?
q.e: 4 full trays hold 40. The 3 oranges left still need one more tray, so 5 trays.

q.t: Rohit has 3 bundles of 10 sticks and 15 loose sticks. How many sticks are there in all?
q.e: 3 bundles = 30. The 15 loose sticks are 1 ten and 5 ones, so 30 + 15 = 45.

q.t: Which is another way of showing 72?
q.e: 12 ones is 1 ten and 2 ones, so 6 tens and 12 ones = 7 tens and 2 ones = 72.

q.t: 5 boats finish a race. The pink boat comes 2nd. How many boats finish after the pink boat?
q.e: The boats after 2nd are 3rd, 4th and 5th — that is 3 boats.

q.t: Surbhi has 34 shells. Each necklace needs 10 shells. How many more shells does she need to make 4 necklaces?
q.e: 4 necklaces need 40 shells. From 34, she needs 6 more to reach 40.

q.t: A shop has 6 packs of 10 balloons and 8 loose balloons. 2 more packs of 10 come in. How many balloons are there now?
q.e: 6 + 2 = 8 packs make 80, and 8 loose balloons make 88.

q.t: I am a two-digit number. My tens digit is 4. My ones digit is 2 more than my tens digit. Who am I?
q.e: Tens digit 4; ones digit 4 + 2 = 6. So the number is 46.

q.t: I am a two-digit number between 60 and 70. My two digits are the same. Who am I?
q.e: Numbers between 60 and 70 have 6 tens, so the ones digit must also be 6.

q.t: What number is 1 ten more than 59?
q.e: Adding 1 ten makes the tens digit go up by 1: 5 tens becomes 6 tens, so 69.

q.t: Meena has 5 tens and 9 ones. Ravi has 6 tens and 0 ones. Who has more?
o: Ravi, because 6 tens is more than 5 tens
Meena, because 9 ones is more than 0 ones
Meena, because she has more ones
q.e: Meena has 59 and Ravi has 60. Compare tens first: 6 tens wins, whatever the ones are.

q.t: Use any two of the cards 4, 9 and 1. What is the biggest two-digit number you can make?
q.e: Put the biggest digit, 9, in the tens place and the next biggest, 4, in the ones place.

q.t: Use any two of the cards 4, 9 and 1. What is the smallest two-digit number you can make?
q.e: Put the smallest digit, 1, in the tens place and the next smallest, 4, in the ones place.

q.t: On a calendar, 15 August is a Tuesday. What is the date of the next Tuesday?
q.e: A week has 7 days, so the same day comes again 7 dates later: 15 + 7 = 22.

q.t: Arya’s jersey number has 1 ten and 7 ones. His friend’s number is 10 more. What is the friend’s number?
q.e: Arya’s number is 17. Adding 10 adds one more ten: 27.
